classification.difficultyReason: Use two right triangles with a shared horizontal distance to relate the flagpole height to the building height.

content.prompt: From the top of a building the angle of depression to the top of a flagpole is $65^{\circ}$. From the base of the building, the angle of elevation to the top of the flagpole is $25^{\circ}$. If the building is 15 metres tall, then determine the height of the flagpole. Give your answer to two decimal places.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 9 diagram in the lower right column
spec.description: Building at left and shorter flagpole at right on common horizontal ground. Preserve both sight lines, upper horizontal reference, vertical extension and both right-angle markers. Coordinates derive from the two given angles and building height; no calculated lengths are printed. Decorative windows, building fill and flag are omitted.
spec.mathematics: The lower sight line makes 25 degrees with the ground. The upper sight line makes a 65-degree angle of depression with the horizontal through the building top. The building height is 15 metres.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the flagpole height and horizontal distance are not supplied.

answer.short:
$2.68\text{ m}$

Use tangent in both right triangles with the same horizontal distance.
answer.worked:
Let $h$ metres be the flagpole height and $d$ metres the horizontal distance between the building and flagpole.
$$\begin{align*}\tan25^{\circ}&=\frac{h}{d}\\h&=d\tan25^{\circ}\\\tan65^{\circ}&=\frac{15-h}{d}\\15-h&=d\tan65^{\circ}\\15&=d(\tan25^{\circ}+\tan65^{\circ})\\d&=\frac{15}{\tan25^{\circ}+\tan65^{\circ}}\\h&=\frac{15\tan25^{\circ}}{\tan25^{\circ}+\tan65^{\circ}}\\h&\approx2.68\end{align*}$$
The flagpole is approximately $2.68\text{ m}$ tall.
